script.title: Big Ben's Clock Is Kept on Time With Old Pennies
sentences: London's most famous clock is kept on time with old pennies.
The Great Clock of Westminster, with its bell Big Ben, was designed by Edmund Beckett Denison and Astronomer Royal George Airy.
It is hand wound three times a week.
It even ran accurately throughout the Blitz.
It keeps time to within a few seconds per week.
The secret sits atop the pendulum: a small stack of pre-decimal pennies.
Add one penny and the pendulum swings faster; each coin added or removed shifts the clock by 0.4 seconds a day.
Had you ever heard of this penny trick?
script.description:
Big Ben's Great Clock is fine-tuned with a stack of old pennies.
One coin shifts it by 0.4 seconds a day.
claims_en: The clock is adjusted by adding or removing pre-decimal pennies on the pendulum.
Big Ben is the nickname for the Great Bell of the Great Clock of Westminster; the tower is the Elizabeth Tower.
The clock was designed by Edmund Beckett Denison and George Airy, the Astronomer Royal.
It is hand wound three times a week.
The clock ran accurately throughout the Blitz.
Big Ben keeps time to within a few seconds per week.
On top of the pendulum is a small stack of pre-decimal penny coins.
Adding a coin increases the rate at which the pendulum swings.
Adding or removing a penny changes the clock's speed by 0.4 seconds per day.
